## Description

A cell of the inner epidermis of a red onion bulb scale: elongated (~200–400 × 40–70 µm), with a
cellulose wall, a huge vacuole coloured by anthocyanins (violet) and the cytoplasm in a thin layer
with the nucleus against the wall. In salt water it loses water and the protoplast detaches from the
wall (plasmolysis), visible without staining.

## In the simulation

<!-- GENERATED:presence -->
Drops: not seeded in the default drops (inoculate it from the Catalogue).

Prepared plates: `onion_epidermis`.
<!-- /GENERATED -->

The protoplast of the `onion_epidermis` [slide](../../mechanics/prepared-plates-and-tissues.md): rows of cellulose
walls and a living protoplast in each, with Boyle–van 't Hoff osmosis (sap ~450 mOsm). It plasmolyses
in salt and recovers in water. Used by the `onion_plasmolysis` lesson.

## Literature

- Classic plant physiology practical (plasmolysis of onion epidermis); Boyle–van 't Hoff relation.
